subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when fitting mixed effect model using factors as independent variables

messages.author: 8dbb28b015bb7762
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error when fitting mixed effect model using factors as independent variables
parts:
Dear Wim,

You are not specifying the model correctly.

You need to create a new variable combining the factors Region and Month,
and assign an 'iid' model to that variable.

This modified code below works as you expect.

best
ï¿½acu.-

Datax <- within(Data, RegionXMonth <- paste(Region, Month, sep = '.'))

formula = Population_Size ~ Month + f(RegionXMonth, model = 'iid')+Region
model_INLA = inla(formula, data=Datax,
family="gaussian",control.predictor = list(link = 1))

fitted_INLA <- model_INLA$summary.fitted.values$mean

plot(as.numeric(Data$Month), Data$Population_Size)
points(as.numeric(Data$Month), fitted_INLA, col="red")
title('Fit INLA')



On 01/10/2014 01:40 PM, W. Konings wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I'm experimenting with the R-INLA package and comparing its results
> with the lme4 package. Fore the model specified in the code below and
> can't get the INLA package to work. It returns me the following error:
>
> Warning message:
> In `[<-.factor`(`*tmp*`, is.na(www), value = 0) :
>
> The code contains 3 blocks:
>
> 1) I simulate a dataset using a simple model specification. I have two
> independent variables (Region and Month) which are both factors. The
> dependent variable is Population Size (which is a numeric variable).
> 2) I fit a mixed effect model using the lme4 package which works fine,
> the fit seems good.
> 3) I try (but fail) to fit the same model using the R-INLA package
>
> Is is clear that the error has something to do with the fact that I
> transform the "month" variable to a factor since I don't get any
> problems when it stays a numerical. My question is very simple: how do
> I avoid the error message that the "inla" function produces? What am I
> doing wrong here?
>
> Thanks,
> W.
>
>
> Code:
>
>
> rm(list = ls())
> library(INLA)
> library(lme4)
>
> #########################################################################################################
> # Simulate DataSet
> #########################################################################################################
> n=400
>
> a1=100
> b1=10
> Data1=data.frame(Region=rep(1,n), Month=sample(1:12, n, replace=TRUE))
> set.seed(1)
> Data1$Population_Size=a1+b1*Data1$Month+rnorm(n)*1
>
> a2=150
> b2=4
> Data2=data.frame(Region=rep(2,n), Month=sample(1:12, n, replace=TRUE))
> set.seed(20)
> Data2$Population_Size=a2+b2*Data2$Month+rnorm(n)*2
>
> a3=5
> b3=20
> Data3=data.frame(Region=rep(3,n), Month=sample(1:12, n, replace=TRUE))
> set.seed(32)
> Data3$Population_Size=a3+b3*Data3$Month+rnorm(n)*3
>
> Data=rbind(Data1,Data2,Data3)
> Data$Region=as.factor(Data$Region)
> Data$Month=as.factor(Data$Month)
>
> #########################################################################################################
> # lme4
> #########################################################################################################
>
> model_lme4=lmer(Population_Size ~ Month+(Region | Month)+Region,
> data=Data)
>
> plot(as.numeric(Data$Month),Data$Population_Size)
> points(as.numeric(Data$Month), fitted(model_lme4), col="red")
> title('Fit lme4')
>
>
> #########################################################################################################
> # INLA
> #########################################################################################################
>
> formula = Population_Size ~ Month+f(Region, Month)+Region
> model_INLA = inla(formula, data=Data,
> family="gaussian",control.predictor = list(link = 1))
